title: Commitment signal + surcharge heuristics (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose / context:
This is a quick personal scratchpad exploring a hybrid pricing primitive: lightweight customer commitment signals + automatic surcharge heuristics for bursts. Goal: get a simple, actionable rule-set we can test in experiments (pricing page, billing UI, pilot contract language). Not polished — lots of heuristics and back-of-envelope math below.

Assumptions (back-of-envelope inputs):
- Typical serving config: quantized 13B-ish model on a single A100-equivalent GPU.
- Amortized infra+gpu cost to Redwood (reserved) = $2.50 / GPU-hour. (includes host, power, basic infra ops)
- Effective steady-state throughput for target model = 150 tokens/sec per GPU (average across prompt/response mix).
- Orchestration + infra overhead (k8s, network, logging, KV caching, control plane) = equivalent of +1.8x on top of GPU cost for short/fragmented sessions. (so total cost multiplier = 2.8x)
- Cold-start / scheduling overhead for a new allocation (where we cannot reuse cached KV) ~ $0.10 amortized per cold invocation (rough heuristic).
- Desired gross margin target = 50% at product level (pre-sales/support).

Core derived numbers:
- GPU $/second = 2.50 / 3600 = $0.0006944/s
- Cost per token (GPU only) = 0.0006944 / 150 = $0.000004629 per token = $0.004629 per 1k tokens.
- Apply infrastructure multiplier (x2.8): total cost per 1k tokens = $0.004629 * 2.8 = $0.01296 ≈ $0.013 per 1k tokens.
- Add cold-start dilution and small-request overhead: for very short sessions (avg < 200 tokens) add an effective +$0.005 per 1k tokens. (This is a hacky amortization.)
- Net unit cost (base) ≈ $0.018 per 1k tokens.
- With 50% gross margin target => suggested list price ≈ $0.036 per 1k tokens (round to $0.035 / 1k for UI simplicity).

Observations on scale & sensitivity:
- If throughput improves to 300 tok/s (better kernels/packing), GPU-only cost per 1k halves -> base unit cost moves to ~ $0.009 per 1k -> price floor with margin ~$0.018 / 1k. So kernel/comp improvement gives obvious leverage.
- If infra overhead is higher (x4) then base unit cost ~ $0.020 / 1k -> price floor ~$0.04 / 1k. So infra amortization matters a lot for low-latency fragmentary workloads.

Commitment signal primitive (rough design):
- Customers can signal a monthly commit (dollars) and an expected sustained concurrency (C). In exchange they receive: lower per-1k token list price and preferential scheduling/burst pool. Commitments are not strict capacity reservations (unless they buy Dedicated) but give a financial preference.
- Pricing tiers:
   - Soft-commit micro: $500/mo -> 10% off list (list = $0.035/1k -> committed price = $0.0315/1k). Bursts allowed up to 2x baseline at 1.25x price.
   - Soft-commit standard: $5k/mo -> 18% off -> $0.0287/1k. Bursts up to 3x at 1.2x price + priority routing.
   - Signal-plus (higher): $25k/mo -> 30% off -> $0.0245/1k. Bursts up to 5x at 1.15x price, SLA uplift (99.9%) and contact in Console.
- Surcharge heuristics: when actual usage in a rolling 1-hour window exceeds (committed baseline * burst_threshold), surcharge applies to overage tokens. Surcharge multiplier = base_surcharge * (observed_ratio ^ slope).
   - Example params: base_surcharge = 1.2 (20% extra), slope = 0.5 (square-root ramp).
   - If committed baseline = X tokens/hour, observed = 4X, ratio = 4 -> surcharge multiplier = 1.2 * (4^0.5) = 1.2 * 2 = 2.4x on excess tokens.
- Rationale: prevents free spikes that kill batching efficiency and force immediate capacity spin-ups; gives predictable penalty curve rather than cliffy overage rates.

Per-session credit idea (session-anchored pricing):
- For UX products (chat, multi-turn), users think in sessions not tokens. Offer "session credits" bundled into commitment packs.
- Define a session credit = ~1k tokens (rounded). Price session credit approximate = token-price per 1k * discount. At our base list $0.035/1k, session credit list = $0.035.
- Tier example: 1k-session-pack (1000 session credits) = priced with volume discount to smooth churn.
- Advantage: easier sales conversations, predictable per-user costs for PMs, less focus on raw tokens (better PLG conversion).

Examples & worked math:
- Small startup: expected monthly 25M tokens. At list $0.035/1k -> bill = 25,000 * 0.035 = $875. (This feels low; signals we should sanity-check inputs vs market comps.)
- Under commit standard ($5k/mo with 18% discount), committed price = $0.0287/1k -> same usage bill = 25,000 * 0.0287 = $717.5. Commitment gives small absolute savings; main value is priority and headroom for growth.
- Heavy-burst example: committed baseline = 10M tokens/month (~333k tokens/day). A sudden campaign doubles hourly traffic for 3 hours (6x local peak). Excess tokens charged at surcharge curve above. That surcharge quickly makes the incremental token price ~2-3x unit price so customer feels friction and we avoid being crushed on unit economics.

Edge cases / practical heuristics:
- Free tier tiny usage: we should impose minimal per-request overhead credit or convert very small bursts into a per-call micro-fee to discourage many tiny chat sessions that blow up scheduling.
- Unpredictable RL / streaming workloads: treat streaming-length responses as different bucket and price by minute of GPU time as well as tokens (hybrid) to reflect runtime impact.
- Embeddings and reranking: cheaper per-1k token cost on inference due to different model sizes and batching characteristics; don't expose same price across all workloads. Instead, have workload-specific floors and discounts.

Operational concerns (what to instrument):
- Track rolling-hour token ratio vs committed baseline per account.
- Breakdown of tokens by session length bins (<200, 200-1k, >1k) and by cold vs warmed KV reuse.
- Measure tokens/sec distribution (to estimate real throughput and GPU utilization).
- Surface to account owners in Console: current hourly burn vs committed baseline + expected surcharge tail.

Open questions / TO-DOs:
- Validate the A100 $/hr assumption with infra finance (is $2.50 realistic after hosting + amortization?).
- Model sensitivity: run simulation of 100k accounts with Pareto usage to estimate how many will spike and what effective margin looks like with surcharge curve.
- UI: how do we show the surcharge curve simply? Maybe a "burst meter" and an explanatory toaster when crossing 1.25x baseline.
- Legal: how to word "soft-commit" in billing docs so customers don't misinterpret it for hard capacity reservation? Need one pager for sales.
- Pricing experiment plan: pick 3 pilot customers, run A/B on discount depth and surcharge slope (slope=0.3,0.5,0.8) for 60 days, instrument churn, NPS, unexpected downtime, and unit-econ.

Quick action items (for me):
- (MAYA) reach out to infra-finance for gated GPU/hr figure (due end of week).
- (ELENA) prototype UI mock for "commitment + burst" page (wireframe).
- (JONAS) script to simulate 10k accounts with Pareto 80/20 and run surcharge math.

Concluding notes:
This feels like a pragmatic middle ground between pay-as-you-go and reserved capacity. Key virtues: easy signal for customers who want price/priority predictability, clear economic disincentive for uncontrolled spikes, and a compact surcharge curve that we can tune without scary cliffs. Biggest risk: if our infra overhead assumptions are wrong, these prices either give away margin or become too expensive. Need quick sims and finance check.
